# Creating a covariance target, optionally by using information from KEGG pathways.

The function `build.target()` is a wrapper function to build the various
types of covariance targets: diagonal ("D"), constant correlation ("F"),
knowledge based ("G", "Gpos", and "Gstar"), correlation ("cor").

## Usage

``` r
build.target(x, genegroups = NULL, type)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  An \\n \times p\\ matrix.

- genegroups:

  List of the groups each gene belongs to: each entry of the list is
  dedicated to a gene (identified the same way as in \\x\\). Each item
  of the list is thus a vector of pathway IDs.

- type:

  Character string specifying the wished target: "D" for a diagonal
  target, "cor" for a correlation target, "G", "Gpos" and "Gstar" for a
  G-type target (see Jelizarow et al, 2010) and "F" for a F-target.

## Value

A \\p \times p\\ target covariance matrix of a certain type.

## References

M. Jelizarow, V. Guillemot, A. Tenenhaus, K. Strimmer, A.-L. Boulesteix,
2010. Over-optimism in bioinformatics: an illustration. Bioinformatics.
Accepted.

## See also

[`targetCor`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetCor.md),
[`targetD`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetD.md),
[`targetF`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetF.md),
[`targetG`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetG.md),
[`targetGpos`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetGpos.md),
[`targetGstar`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/targetGstar.md),.

Other main functions:
[`shrink.estim()`](https://github.com/vguillemot/SHIP/reference/shrink.estim.md)

## Author

Vincent Guillemot

## Examples

``` r

# Simulate dataset
x <- matrix(rnorm(20*30), 20, 30)
# Try different targets
build.target(x, type = "D")
```
